Premise CONFIRMED by inspection of infra/scripts/observability.sh: the `[ "$new" -lt 0 ] && new=$total` clamp is present at six sites — §3 replication_errors (l.103), §4 voter_errors (l.134), §4c review_bot_merge_change_errors (l.158), §4d deploy_errors (l.180), §4e publish_autodeploy_marker_delta (l.213, serving BOTH deploy_deferrals and review_interrupts), §4b g2p_dispatch_errors (l.260). All six now assign 0.

Fix is 6 tokens + one shared rationale comment at §3 with back-references at the other five. No boot-id/cursor state machine and no Python migration: after the change each counter is a subtraction and a clamp, not logic worth porting. A time-windowed rewrite (journalctl --since, deleting the offset files) is the genuinely better long-term shape but changes the metric's semantics under clock skew — out of scope for a latent-hazard bugfix, noted here rather than done.

Bash delta is comment-only; no new bash logic.

Change: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1648

Deployment needs NO manual box action: autodeploy.sh watches OBS_PATHS ('infra/scripts/observability.sh infra/scripts/install-observability.sh') and re-runs the idempotent install-observability.sh on the box on a probe-source change, re-materializing /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh. Landing on main ships it.

Test evidence (AC2): tests/scripts/test_observability_rotation_2dc7.py seeds every offset file to 99 against a 7-marker stub journal (the shrinking-journal simulation) and asserts the published value is 0 for all seven metrics, plus a follow-up assertion that a marker arriving after the reset still publishes as 1 (suppression is not sticky). Confirmed RED against the pre-fix script: all 8 tests fail with 'assert [7] == [0]'; all 8 pass post-fix.

Also updated tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py::test_reset_count_is_retried_after_failed_publish — it asserted [7, 7], i.e. it explicitly encoded the old republish-the-total behaviour. Renamed to test_shrunken_journal_holds_the_offset_across_a_failed_publish and now asserts [0, 0]; its actual contract (a failed publish must not advance the offset) is unchanged and still verified.
